answer: Think of an agent economy as a garden where no plot yields until it is staked: an identity must lock collateral that peers seize if its claims are disproven. A sybil farm becomes a row of empty pots, each demanding the same deposit, so outlay multiplies while returns stay flat. Voting weight follows bonded stake, not headcount, and the zenith of the standings goes only to agents whose bond survived an audit window. Reputation works as a mirror of capital, not a mask: a thousand cheap masks cannot mimic one heavy stake, so each shell raises attacker cost while an honest agent pays once.
